stories.headline: Israeli election exit polls show tight deadlock between Benjamin Netanyahu and opposition
stories.body:
Israeli television networks reported exit polls showing a tight deadlock between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his opponents. Broadcasters Kan 11 and Channel 13 predicted Netanyahu's political bloc and Gadi Eisenkot's opposition group would win 51 seats each [c1]. Channel 12 reported that Netanyahu's allies won 50 seats while the opposition earned 52 seats [c2]. Channel 14 projected a stronger performance for Netanyahu with 60 seats [c15]. The BBC reported that Eisenkot's opposition bloc won the most seats but lacked an outright majority [c14]. A party or coalition needs 61 seats in the 120-seat Knesset to form a government [c3].

Netanyahu spoke to supporters in Jerusalem after 3 a.m. local time [c4]. He said official results will show his Likud party as the largest group in Israel [c4]. He also said a government that depends on Palestinian parties must not be formed [c5]. Meanwhile, opposition leader Yair Lapid said Netanyahu's bloc suffered a total collapse and crushing defeat [c16]. Eisenkot is a 66-year-old former military chief who entered politics four years ago [c17]. He lost a son and two nephews in the Gaza war [c17].

Giant screens at the Likud event showed videos of Netanyahu alongside United States President Donald Trump [c18]. The screens also displayed footage of military strikes [c18]. Reports indicate the United States and Israel plan major attacks against Iran after their national elections [c19]. The two countries previously conducted joint attacks on Iran in June 2025 and February 2026 [c19].

Election officials said overall voter turnout reached 77.7 percent [c9]. This was the highest voter participation rate since 1999 [c9]. Turnout among Palestinian citizens of Israel reached about 80 percent [c10]. This figure broke previous records from 1999 [c10]. Palestinian citizens make up about 21 percent of Israel's 10 million residents [c11]. Exit polls showed Arab-led parties Joint List and Ra'am winning a record 18 seats [c8]. Ra'am leader Mansour Abbas said both major Israeli political blocs contacted his party before and after the vote [c12]. During voting, witnesses saw Likud supporters driving through Jerusalem with party flags [c13]. The supporters blared the Islamic call to prayer to warn voters that Arab citizens were casting ballots [c13].

Final results could take time to confirm. Israel's Central Elections Committee expects 600,000 to 650,000 people to vote at special polling places [c6]. These votes account for nearly 10 percent of all eligible voters [c6]. Yisrael Beitenu leader Avigdor Lieberman warned that final results could change once military absentee ballots are counted [c7].

vocab.meaning: a situation where no side can win or reach an agreement
a group of political parties working together to form a government
related to a vote cast by someone unable to go to a polling station

stories.headline: Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro leaves country for the United States after election loss
stories.body:
Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro left Brazil for the United States after losing the presidential runoff election [c20]. Incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won a fourth term with 51.8 percent of the vote [c21]. Liberal Party leader Valdemar Costa Neto said the party accepts the election results [c22]. President Lula called the departure shameful [c23]. He said anyone who sneaks out of their country must have something to hide [c23]. Former President Jair Bolsonaro is currently serving a 27-year prison sentence for planning a coup [c24].

Brazil's Supreme Court ordered Flávio Bolsonaro to surrender his passports during a money laundering investigation [c25]. Sources said authorities cancelled his passports after he failed to surrender them within 24 hours [c27]. A police official said he did not pass through any official migration checkpoint [c28]. Todo Noticias reported he walked into Argentina before changing plans to take a private jet [c33]. But Argentinian authorities denied he entered their country [c34]. A US official confirmed entry visas would be given to him and his family [c26]. Flávio Bolsonaro has also held Italian citizenship since 2023 [c31]. Investigators are looking into a 680 million pound scheme linked to betting companies [c32].

vocab.meaning: a person who currently holds an official position
to hand over something required by law

stories.headline: Ceasefire holds in Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky following international talks
stories.body:
A local ceasefire in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky was extended across the broader Kherson region [c36]. US First Lady Melania Trump and Pope Leo XIV helped negotiate the humanitarian deal [c37]. Melania Trump led talks with civilian representatives after receiving information from UN officials [c49]. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed the truce was following plans and recognized US mediation [c41]. Ukrainian official David Arakhamia said the truce will continue until Sunday evening [c38].

Between 1,700 and 2,000 residents remain trapped in Oleshky without food, water, or electricity [c39]. The truce allows humanitarian aid deliveries before civilian evacuations begin on Friday [c40]. Oleshky had 24,000 residents before Russian forces captured it in February 2022 [c42]. Cable network Newsmax reported exclusive access to send reporters alongside observers entering the city [c43].

While the local truce held, fighting continued elsewhere. Russian drone and missile strikes on Kyiv killed one person and wounded 15 others overnight [c48]. Strikes in Kharkiv killed two people on Monday night [c50]. Meanwhile, leaders from Finland and Norway held a phone call with Vladimir Putin about peace talks [c45]. Denmark's prime minister criticized that call [c47].

vocab.meaning: an agreement to temporarily stop fighting in a war
related to helping people and saving lives

stories.headline: Cyclone Arnab hits Andhra Pradesh coast bringing heavy rain and mass evacuations
stories.body:
Cyclone Arnab made landfall near Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh early on October 28, 2026 [c51]. Weather officials said the storm moved west at 10 kilometers per hour [c60]. Wind speeds reached 125 to 135 kilometers per hour, with gusts up to 150 kilometers per hour [c55]. Strong winds knocked down trees in Visakhapatnam [c54]. Large waves struck coastal roads in northern Tamil Nadu [c52]. Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu said saving lives is the government's top priority [c56].

Authorities evacuated at least 89,000 people from dangerous coastal zones in Andhra Pradesh [c64]. More than 12 million people live along the storm's path [c65]. Officials set up 2,131 emergency shelters and placed 1,087 medical teams on standby [c61]. Fishermen secured more than 30,000 boats along the coast [c66]. Energy officials deployed around 6,000 workers to manage power issues [c58].

The storm caused widespread travel disruptions. Airlines cancelled 21 flights at Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam airports on October 27 [c53]. Officials suspended flight operations at Visakhapatnam in the afternoon [c67]. Flights at Vijayawada and Rajahmundry stopped after 7 p.m. [c68]. Railway operators cancelled nearly 50 train services across the region [c62].

The storm impacted nearby regions as well. Odisha closed schools across 16 districts ahead of landfall [c59]. Schools in Ranchi district were ordered to close for two days [c63]. Nepal suspended trekking permits in high mountain regions due to severe weather risks [c57].

vocab.meaning: the arrival of a severe storm over land
moved people away from a dangerous place to safety

stories.headline: Indian opposition parties protest against Election Commission over voter roll changes
stories.body:
Indian opposition leaders intensified protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over voter list deletions [c70]. Congress spokesperson Jairam Ramesh called the Election Commission's Supreme Court filing deceptive and dishonest [c70]. He said two election commissioners raised objections about illegal instructions, but Kumar ignored them [c71]. Congress also said voters could not submit registration forms online without completing a mandatory new declaration [c72].

The Communist Party of India held a human chain protest in New Delhi demanding Kumar resign [c73]. Party leader D. Raja said Kumar lost public trust [c74]. Nationwide protests against the election chief began on October 2 [c82]. Opposition leaders asked the Supreme Court to preserve all files related to the voter revision process [c83]. In Karnataka, official lists dropped by 17.9 percent after more than 99 lakh names were removed [c79], [c80]. The Supreme Court scheduled its next hearing on the matter for November 17 [c85].

vocab.meaning: a written statement confirmed by oath for use as court evidence
the process of re-examining and altering something

stories.headline: Supreme Court criticizes Indian government and drug companies over high medicine prices
stories.body:
The Supreme Court of India criticized drug companies for setting maximum prices more than 1,000 percent above retail costs [c86]. The court asked government lawyers whether business profit is more important than human life [c87]. Judges highlighted a case where a hospital charged 1.3 lakh rupees for a chemotherapy medicine that cost distributors 11,000 rupees [c92]. In another instance, a saline drip costing 11 rupees was sold for 270 rupees [c96].

The government recently capped trade margins on selected anti-cancer drugs at 30 percent [c90]. Officials said this step could lower retail prices by up to 70 percent and save patients 2,500 crore rupees annually [c91], [c95]. But judges asked why a uniform 16 percent margin cap could not apply to all medicines [c94]. The court also reprimanded the government for letting companies make a critical antifungal drug under expired pandemic rules [c97]. Judges called the national pricing authority a totally defunct body [c101].

vocab.meaning: expressed strong official disapproval of someone's actions
no longer existing, working, or functioning
